key_insight: The paper presents a computer-assisted framework that proves global regularity for continuous families of 3D periodic Navier-Stokes flows by combining finite reference trajectories with a shared, parameter-uniform error bound.
engineering_relevance: This gives computational fluid dynamics researchers a reusable way to certify smoothness across flow families, including parameter ranges beyond standard smallness criteria, which is valuable for rigorous simulation and model validation.
method: Build finite reference trajectories and retain the full nonlinear residual before spectral truncation.
Use a common error bound to cover an interval of center fields plus infinitely many smooth perturbation modes.
Extend the proof until viscous decay guarantees regularity for all later times.
evidence_signal: The study reports applications to cyclic-shear, Arnold-Beltrami-Childress, and Taylor-Green flows, plus an ensemble of 4,096 configurations and 1,600 refinement trajectories with public turbulence data and neural-operator experiments.
watch_item: The certification depends on carefully constructed reference trajectories and bounds, so scaling the approach to new flow families may require substantial compute and proof-specific tuning.
paper_title: Computer-assisted global regularity across nonlinear families of three-dimensional periodic Navier-Stokes flows
